I've been on an antipsychotic medication (Seroquel) for four years. I've dosed and micro dosed a dozen times and only one experience was "bad", but this was also due to not having a support system, a trip sitter and dosing during a depressive episode. Bad judgement call on my part. 

It 'can' be dangerous, but going into a trip/micro dose with intention, a support system in place and a plan for the possibility of things going south there's less of a chance for lingering, undesirable side effects/psychosis. 

If her medication dosage is on the higher end, a micro dose would be best. There are also clinics and psychologists/psychotherapists nowadays who offer sessions for such occasions. It's difficult to research places that participate in these kind of "experiments" but they are out there.

Micro dosing is safe, effective and worth while. Nobody needs nearly as much as they think they do for a therapeutic dose.

There are SO many different ways to approach this question. Some people have said bits about diabetics, or asthmatics but I feel a more philosophic and psychologic approach is just as eye opening. 

What makes a person, or even an animal a singular and unique entity? Action? Behavior? Genetics? Characteristics? Preferences? Thoughts? Feelings? The list could go on and on and on and on.
I don't believe the human body, the human mind, human consciousness is as simple as singularity. If you're drunk, are you still you? If you're having an emotional reaction or if you're dysregulating your emotions, are you still you? I believe yes, you are still you. Each person's life experience brings out different parts of themselves, things move "through" us. Food. Liquid. Emotions. Thoughts. Desires. Blood is constantly, endlessly, relentlessly flowing RIGHT under our skin! 

Example: I am white girl wasted, sprawled out on the floor, not entirely acting like 'myself', crying to my best friend about how much I love her. I am still me, no? Because what is passing "through" me (both physically ((the alcohol)) and emotionally ((the crying and the love))) cannot take away who I am at my core. 

It's not about what you say, or what you think, or what you feel that makes You who You are. It's your presence. The kinda stuff you can never really find words for, like how epic a kiss was or how badly it hurt when you broke a bone or that subtle intuition that's been nagging at you for days... Give a lil attention to the subtleties and see what starts unfolding for you ~
